[USER] User inquired about the significance of presidential executive orders in the US political system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Presidential executive orders hold a significant role in the US political system's functioning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Executive orders allow the president to establish policies and guidelines that are binding on federal agencies and government departments.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Executive orders can take effect immediately, meaning they can have an immediate impact on the country.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Executive orders are subject to judicial review, and if they violate the Constitution, they can be struck down by the courts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Executive orders can limit the power of Congress by establishing policies and guidelines that are beyond the scope of Congress's authority.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Presidential executive orders ensure continuity of governance, even during transitions of power.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, presidential executive orders provide the president with a powerful tool to govern quickly and efficiently, but they also expose the US political system to a potential risk of executive overreach.  
[USER] User asked if executive orders can be used to make major changes in the law without the approval of Congress.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yes, executive orders can be used to make major changes in law without the approval of Congress.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The scope and extent of changes that can be made through executive orders are limited by the Constitution and judicial review.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Executive orders can clarify or carry out existing laws, but they cannot contradict or usurp the authority of Congress to create new laws.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If an executive order goes beyond the president's constitutional powers or is inconsistent with the legislative will of Congress, it can be challenged and overturned through judicial review.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Executive orders can have significant effects on public policy, and presidents have used them to enact a range of significant policies, including immigration policy, regulatory policy, and social policy.  
[USER] User asked if the use of executive orders undermines the checks and balances system in the US political system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The use of executive orders has been a topic of debate and controversy around the balance of power and the checks and balances system in the US political system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some argue that the use of executive orders undermines the checks and balances system by giving the president excessive power without the need for approval or cooperation from Congress or the judiciary.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This can potentially lead to abuses of power and disregard for the separation of powers that is central to the US democratic system
